The initial project involves analyzing approximately 560,000 individual prices across approximately 9,000 SKUs.

This is not a traditional financial analysis or accounting role. The primary challenge is analytical: understanding a very large and complex pricing dataset, identifying the patterns and logic behind it, separating meaningful commercial differences from unnecessary complexity and historical exceptions, and developing a clearer and more manageable pricing structure.

The ideal candidate is someone who can take a large, messy dataset, impose structure on it, identify what matters, ask the right business questions, and translate the analysis into clear recommendations for executive leadership.

• Develop logical categorization and segmentation frameworks across products, customers, channels, pricing groups, or other relevant dimensions.

• Form and test hypotheses to understand why pricing varies and whether those differences continue to make business sense.

• Recommend opportunities to simplify, standardize, consolidate, or redesign pricing structures while preserving important commercial distinctions.

• Transform large and complex datasets into clear business insights and actionable recommendations.

• Build analytical models, tools, dashboards, or datasets to support pricing analysis and ongoing decision-making.

• Partner directly with the CFO on strategic pricing and commercial decisions.

• Present findings clearly and concisely to executive leadership and other stakeholders.
